title: Who wrote Pretty Baby and local songwriters
summary: The group tries to identify the writer of Pretty Baby and discusses local songwriters like Virgis and Klessy.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. I've got a note here that asks who wrote Pretty Baby.
Do you remember that tune? Yeah, I remember Pretty Baby. Yeah, I remember it quite well. We played it every night there. But who wrote it, I don't know.
Was it somebody in the band? Supposed to be a local writer?
I thought I was a baby, but I remember. Was it somebody in the band? Do you remember that? I don't believe. I don't believe somebody.
Was it a local writer that wrote it? That's what I'm asking.
Unless it was this guy, Virgis. Billy Virgis. He wrote some things. Louis Virgis. Louis Virgis, yeah.
And you have another one down here that used to write songs. He was a good friend of Pinky's. What the hell was his name?
Al Josen, you mean? The one we used to call Al Josen? Did he play? No, he was strictly a songwriter.
He used to write the politician songs? No, no, no, no. You wrote a lot of things.
You had Joe Virgis and Klessy and Erwin LeClar. It might have been Klessy wrote that Pretty Baby.
I don't know. We can look it up. He was a pretty good songwriter because he was fortunate.
Chris Yassich. No, no, no. Chris used to want to write the parodies on the tunes for Paul Tugas.

I remember him saying that with Pinky when he would write a thing, don't worry if it's not going to be a hit. Because he says if it gets on the record and if the flip side is a hit, he says you got a hit too. So, I mean, he wrote a lot of things that he just wanted to get on record. And he had one of them on the one side of Andrew's sister's record that he did very well. I can't remember his name. He used to, he was a publisher from, he used to have a publishing company.

Yeah, I remember the one that was running out was Chris, not Chris. No, Sig Christian's his old lady. That's the one you're talking about. I can't remember his name. I can't remember his name. I can't remember his name.

What about this note about Columbia's tunes, Dick? I just wondered if they pushed any tunes. But you, we went over that, didn't we? Yeah. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Crum knew all that. Yeah. We still didn't finish with what happened to the leaders of the band. You and, you and...
